utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, good morning, Mr. Registrar. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is case number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And good morning to you. Mr. Oric, can you follow the proceedings in your own language.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Please sit down. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Good morning Your Honours I'm Patricia Sellers representing the Prosecution. Today with me is co-counsel, Mr. Jose Doria, and our case manager, Mrs. Donnica Henry-Frijlink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you and good morning to you madam and to your team. Appearances for Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. I am Vasvija Vidovic, and together with Mr. John Jones I represent Mr. Naser Oric. Together with us, our legal assistant Miss Adisa Mehic, and our case manager, Mr. Geoff Roberts. And good morning to our learned colleagues from the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, madam, and good morning to you and your team. I am experiencing, in my headphones a lot of background voices, and B/C/S in particular. I don't know if I am on the right channel. I mean, that's not a problem. I don't know if it's just me or if it's ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: It's better now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. For me it is worse now. I am hearing one particular person, A woman's voice translating what I am saying into B/C/S. So it's only me? It's the chairman's privilege? You too? You must be aspiring to become chairman. So -- I don't know. We can carry on, it is not disturbing me that much. I wanted to make sure it didn't disturb the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not experiencing that problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Neither are we, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. So any preliminaries before we go into videolink?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour the only preliminary to announce is that we will be going forward with the next witness and we would ask that it would be done between a break in the court sessions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I thank you. Mr. Jones, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No preliminaries, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. So let's connect with wherever the witness is by videolink and proceed with her testimony

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I am not being interpreted at the moment, but could the interpreters who were interpreting before continue interpreting as if under normal circumstances so that I see whether I can hear their voices as well.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Testing, 1, 2, 3, 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, that's not what I meant. What I meant is, interpreting while I am speaking, in other words as you were doing before, during the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm doing it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I think it seems to be fine. Now may I ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, it's not. It's not. I can still hear the interpretation. I can still hear the interpretation. Anyway, let's proceed while they deal with the problem. Let's go into videolink, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Good morning. I want to make sure that you are receiving us.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So you have tested the microphone as well. Good morning to you. Is the witness present?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you can bring her in and we can proceed with her cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Good morning, Madam Stamenic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Welcome back. We are going to proceed and conclude -- proceed with and conclude the cross-examination this morning. So before the next break, this should be all over and you will be able to return home. I just wanted to remind you of the solemn declaration that you entered yesterday, which is still valid and binding for today's continued testimony of yours. I also would like to remind you that if at any time there are problems with interpretation or with the visual transmission, to please draw our attention straight away, either directly or through the intervention of the -- of Madam Registrar, who is there with you in the room. Did I make myself clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, Mr. Jones will continue with his cross-examination now. Thank you. Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, thank you Your Honour. I must say I had difficulty just hearing the witness's responses there, or the interpretation of the responses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please do tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can I -- let me ask the witness to say something again. In my case, it was okay. I mean, I was receiving interpretation and I could even hear her.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. Well I can start and if there is any problem I will immediately draw it to your attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Stamenic. Good morning, firstly.

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is it okay, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, I want to start with a clarification or two of what you testified about yesterday, specifically in relation to Djemila, the Muslim woman who was a friend of your family before the war. Now, first of all, what was her last name, if you could help us with that?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sorry could you repeat your answer, please?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. I heard her saying "ne znam" which would be "I don't know," and it was interpreted as "no." But perhaps it comes to the same thing. Could you help us with how old she was at the time, in January 1993, approximately?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was in her middle ages.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, you told us yesterday that she wasn't living in Dobrak at the time. Firstly, how did you know that?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because they were refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And how do you know that they were refugees?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had been expelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you know who they had been expelled by?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, you saw her at or around 6.00 a.m. on the morning of the 16th of January, 1993, by your house. Were you surprised to see her there at that time?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Did you speak to her while she was dressing your wounds or while she was waiting with you, before you were loaded on the ox cart, and find out what her situation was and where she was staying?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Are there woods near your hamlet or where -- your former hamlet, if you're not living there now?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Did she not tell you that she and others had had to go and live in the woods after they'd been expelled?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. So you don't know where she was living at that time?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now you wouldn't describe her as a soldier, would you?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And Ismet, the postman whom you've described, he was also a civilian; correct?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So it's right, isn't it, that when you came to your house and you saw it burning, that there were civilians there in the vicinity of your house as well as what you've described as soldiers?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And isn't it true that there were great many civilians in the vicinity of your house when you came back?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both civilians and soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. And a great many civilians, would you agree?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were many.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, going back to where we left off yesterday, when we left off you arrived in Srebrenica and you'd been taken to the hospital, and this was on the 17th of January, 1993. How long did you stay in the hospital for?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I stayed there while my wounds were being dressed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Just to give us a rough idea, was it an hour, two hours? More? Less?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe half an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, you had an opportunity, didn't you, to observe the conditions in the hospital? Would you agree that the conditions were appalling?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not looking.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, did you see other patients there in the hospital?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: The personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Wasn't there in the hospital a terrible smell of unwashed bodies and illness?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I would like to read an extract from a book which is an exhibit in this case, for your reaction. You won't have it in front of you and you don't need it in front of you, but it's D199, "war hospital," pages 93 to 94 for our reference. And This describes a visit to Srebrenica hospital by a doctor from MSF, in December 1992. So a month or so before you were there. On page 93, third paragraph, it's written: "On each bed lies a patient, on each patient lies a dirty, stained bed sheet, that is all. No IV bags drip. No machines beep. No bottles of medicine sit on the night stands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Jones, what time, particular time is that quote related to?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: December 1992. So just about a month before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, first do you agree that conditions in the hospital were as dirty and primitive as described in that section?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It was nothing like a modern hospital, was it?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Would you agree it was nothing like -- sorry. We have a technical issue. It was nothing like as nice and clean and modern and well-equipped as the hospital in Uzice where you were treated in Serbia after your release?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And while you'd been treated in Uzice, isn't it right that that's also where VRS soldiers and other Serb soldiers were treated, if you noticed that?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, going back to this extract, page 93: "On one of the beds a small girl lies crying. Eric," and that's the foreign doctor being shown around the hospital, "sees that she has a broken arm where there should be a cast put on the arm and helping it heal, two tree branches are affixed with scotch tape." Now, pausing there, would you agree that that describes a similar situation to yours, perhaps, less than adequate treatment being provided for, but the doctors doing their best under very difficult circumstances? Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And finally, and it is turning the page, page 94: "The most vivid image in his mind is of that crying little girl with her pathetic homemade splint. They could have devised something better for her," he thinks. "All of it lends the impression of a medical team so overwhelmed by the situation that they are no longer able to see what they can achieve. They've all but given up". Now you were there in that hospital in January 1993 and treated by these doctors in Srebrenica, did you get that impression, that they were doing their very best for you, but that they were burnt out and lacking equipment?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And finally on that theme, you didn't have the impression, did you, that you received any inferior treatment because you were a Serb?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, you did tell us yesterday that when were you in the hospital a soldier came and kicked you because there was a dead Muslim soldier, and he somehow held you responsible for the death of that soldier. And then another soldier made him stop. Now a question or two about that. Is that what you told ICTY investigators when you were interviewed by them on the 25th of May, 2000?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, I put it to you that that's not what you said. That in 2000, when you spoke to investigators about this, you said that it was a civilian who kicked you and a civilian who made him stop. Do you accept that that's what you might have said?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: A doctor made him do that. He wore a white coat. I stated that a doctor in a white coat took him out of that room.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. So that's firstly a correction of what you said yesterday: It wasn't a soldier who made him stop. It was a doctor.

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: A doctor, a man in a white coat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Doria.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: First of all, I don't recall the witness saying yesterday that a soldier stopped the other one from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't recall either.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We should check the transcript. It's precisely what she said.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: I cannot find it. She said someone kicked but she didn't say about anyone stopping.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We can check. We can check.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Is it necessary to check it now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know. But once an objection has been raised ... I don't recollect the witness saying that a soldier then stopped her -- stopped the other soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If Your Honours will give me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I do recollect her saying that a soldier kicked her, that for sure. But I don't recollect the other statement. And I'm stopping here because, you know, you are using it as a platform to attack the consistency in her testimony, so.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Seeking to clarify it in any event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. Otherwise I would have bypassed it, because to me it is not that important.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, what I have is, it's page 31, line 4 and that "when he kicked you, this other soldier swore." There was a reference to two soldiers. That's in the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There was one soldier, Mr. Jones. Always one soldier. The question was, I intervened at one point in time because when Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. she was asked to explain how he swore, in fact the transcript that Mr. Doria was using, "swore to her," and I corrected it, "swore at her," and she gave an explanation that not referred to swearing at all and then I tried to point that out. But anyway, let's move. I don't think at this point in time it is much, that much relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: What is more important is who did the kicking and I will move on to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes, Mr. Doria.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: As Your Honours correctly pointed out, that it has to do with the credibility of the witness and if she didn't say that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But -- point taken. It was put to the witness that she had stated that and we are coming to the conclusion that we can't find it anyway. Let's take a neutral stand about it, but the matter ends there. It's --

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It has never occurred now. So, yes, Mr. Jones, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. I would like to refer you to your statement in 2000 and you don't have it in front of you, but for our benefit it is pages 2 to 3 and the ERN is 00998369 to 00998370: "At the hospital I was kept on a stretcher at the waiting room and a dead body of a Muslim soldier was also kept on a stretcher next to me. A civilian came to me and told that I had carried a rifle and had killed that soldier lying next to me. He kicked me having said that." Then you went on to say, "another civilian who had a black beard came and took the one who had kicked me out of the waiting room". Now you accepted yesterday that your statement in 2000 was a truthful statement. Do you also accept that in May 2000, nearly five years ago, you had a better recollection of events than you do now?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And do you accept, hearing what you said five years ago, that in fact it was a civilian who kicked you in the hospital and not a soldier?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Very well. Now from the hospital you were taken to the SUP, you told us, to join your mother and then you were taken together to the Detention Centre behind the courthouse. The whole time you were being carried on a stretcher, correct?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And no one mistreated you either at the police station or on the way to the Detention Centre?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now the people who took you from the hospital to the SUP, they weren't wearing red bands around their head, were they?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, you said yesterday that the same people took you from Kusici to the hospital and then to the Detention Centre. You don't in fact have a clear recollection of that, do you?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. How many of them were there, firstly?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: A few.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, could you tell us the precise number, if you have a clear recollection?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Can you tell us anything about them at all, about their names, physical description?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Are you saying that all of these people accompanied you all the way from Kusici, stayed over night, and then took you to the hospital and then to the Detention Centre? Or only some of them?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not all of them. Just a few of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You can't tell us how many people there were?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. I put it to you, and I think the suggestion is probably clear, but in fact you have no clear recollection of any specific individuals accompanying you all the way?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there were a few of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We move now to the Detention Centre where you were held for about 20 days. Now, firstly, you're aware, weren't you, that there was no electricity in Srebrenica at the time?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no electricity at the place where we stayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. So it was pitch black at night then.

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And you didn't have candles or anything like that which you burnt at night to provide light?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And this was mid-winter, correct, so it was actually dark for a large portion of the night? Very dark for a large portion of the night.

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, would it be fair to summarise your treatment at the Detention Centre in this way: That the conditions there were certainly basic, but that you were never beaten or otherwise physically mistreated?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So in other words, nobody ever touched a hair on your head the whole time that you were at the Detention Centre?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And the same applies, doesn't, it, to all of the other women with whom you were imprisoned?

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, what's the problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Just in connection with what my learned friend was saying about she never being mistreated. If you recall, Your Honour, the witness testified yesterday that someone came in and pointed a pistol into her head and she was very frightened because of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: This is pure argument, it is for the witness to reply if she considers that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. But it's a valid, a very valid point that is being raised by Mr. Doria. That calls for some clarification from the witness. I mean, because -- the way she is describing the events now, it's as if, I mean, would exclude anything like she described yesterday having ever -- having ever happened. Anyway, do proceed with your question. Do proceed with your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And with your next question and then we will come to the point raised by Mr. Doria, we will just ask for a confirmation or a denial from the witness as regards to that particular event.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. My question and the subsequent one are dealing with physical mistreatment in the sense that actual physical contact --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I understand. This is why I'm telling you to proceed with your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The same applies, doesn't it, to the other women with whom you were imprisoned - leaving any threats which might have been made aside - you never saw any of them being physically mistreated, manhandled or beaten during the whole 20 days that you were there; correct?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And it's correct, isn't it, that since you were in the stretcher, you were actually in that cell for 24 hours a day for the whole of those 20 days?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And you didn't see either, did you, any sign on the women that they had been mistreated when they left the cell and then came back for questioning? Or rather when they left for questioning and came back?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Actually the answer is "yes," I didn't see any.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You were asked yesterday about women being taken for interrogation, which I think you will -- we can all agree sounds rather sinister. In fact, they were taken, asked some questions, and brought back to the cell, as far as you could tell. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were taken out and brought back to the cell.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. And when they came back they showed no signs of having been mistreated?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, you told how you were given food every day, and obviously it was not a great quantity. But were you aware at the time that people in Srebrenica in fact didn't receive any more food than you, in fact many had a lot less? Is that something you were told or became aware of?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sorry, I think there might have been a mistake in the interpretation. I was referring to the people in Srebrenica. Not Zenica, receiving less food than you, whether you were aware of the refugees in Srebrenica suffering from severe food shortages?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So no one ever said to you, in relation to the food you were receiving, "We don't get much better?" i.e., a Muslim saying they in fact don't receive much more food than you were getting?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Naser Oric came. He introduced himself and he told us that they themselves were not getting any more than us.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So in fact you did hear that the people in Srebrenica were not receiving any more food than you?

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may raise an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: The witness was testifying about Naser Oric, who was the commander. It seems as if he identified himself. I wonder if this implies that he is saying about if the witness is talking about the people in general or only the soldiers, the Muslim soldiers? I think it needs a clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But if the witness is stating, Mr. Doria, that the person who introduced himself as Naser Oric told her that they were not receiving any more food than her, "they" means, basically, at least us that how I interpret it, the people in -- the Muslims in Srebrenica. So at the end of the day, what's the basis of your objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Well I thought the witness was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There is one person who told you "we are in the same position." So at the end of the day she did hear that the Muslims were in the same position, or in the same predicament as she was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: My interpretation, Your Honour, is that the witness was referring to the soldiers. I mean the ones who were holding them in captivity. Not generally people.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I don't think the Prosecution's interpretation of the evidence is a good ground for an objection. If the point that my learned friend wants to take in re-examination --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Keep moving, Mr. Jones. I don't see any validity in your objection. It's a question as it has been rightly pointed out, it's a question of interpretation and that's it. Mr. Jones, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: In fact, due to the objection, I note that the witness's answer, which was "yes" as I heard it to the question so in fact you did hear that the people in Srebrenica were not receiving any more food than you, didn't appear on the record. So I think I need to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Put the question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So, Ms. Stamenic, in contrast to what you told us earlier, you did in fact hear that the people in Srebrenica or at least some of them were no better position than you?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The witness replied yes again and I'm afraid it is not appearing. May I first have the answer of the witness on the record. It is rather frustrating she has twice said "yes," and ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We need the answer on the transcript. I clearly heard her say "yes" in reply to Mr. Jones question. Does that suffice, Mr. Jones? I think it does suffice.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Let's ask the witness. Ms. Stamenic, can you just repeat the word you said again, nice and clearly.

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I simply don't understand why the interpretation is ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Judge Eser.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Just to clarify, the question was --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I just wonder if we should solve the technical problem first because it might become very confusing. The witness has said three times and it hasn't once --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: That's not my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I wonder if we should solve that first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: That's clear. My question was, is that you asked the witness who told us earlier you did in fact hear that the people in Srebrenica or at least some of them were not in any better position than you. And the witness answered "yes." Now my question is, from whom did you hear this? Who told you that the people in Srebrenica are not in a better position than you are? Who told you this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Stamenic, could you answer the question, please. Who -- Judge Eser's question is a very simple one. Who told you that the people in Srebrenica, or at least some of them, were not in any better position than you were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. The other thing is, you very rightly pointed out, Mr. Jones, that on the two or three occasions the witness did say -- answer "yes" and on each of these three occasions we did not find the word, the translation. We didn't see "yes" scrolling in the text in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. I'm prepared to move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think we ought to. The other thing I wanted to correct is that, in your last question to the witness, you sort of -- let me find it. Yes. Your last question to the witness started with "Ms. Stamenic in contrast to what you told us earlier, you did in fact hear that the people in Srebrenica, or at least some of them, were in no better position than you". I don't like particularly the way you put it, as if there is a contrast to -- with what she had stated earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: But the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Earlier the question was whether she was aware that the people in Srebrenica, the refugees in Srebrenica were suffering from severe food shortages and her answer was "I didn't know." So not knowing is one thing. Having heard about food shortages is another. So, but let's move on. I just wanted to put it on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And as far as this being told to you by Naser Oric is concerned -- firstly, you didn't know anyone called Naser Oric before the war, did you?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. You told us yesterday, when this person came and announced themselves as -- or introduced themselves as being Naser Oric, that was effectively your basis for saying that it was Naser Oric; correct? You based yourself on what he announced rather than any recognition?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of the fact that he introduced himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. You didn't recognise him as Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Just on that theme still, when this person who introduced himself, as Naser Oric came into your cell, did you have a clear view of him?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I could see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You could see him from your stretcher as he came through the door?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him when he came in.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So it was light in your cell at that time?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So it was during the day, wasn't it, that this person came in?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, going back to the conditions in your cell, you mentioned how the other women would be taken to the toilet sometimes. But they could also relieve themselves in this bucket in their cell, couldn't they, if they needed to?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you remember the cooks who came and gave you food? Do you remember the names of any of those cooks?

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Doria.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: I have an objection to the -- my learned friend the way in which he puts the question, if you remember the cooks who came in and gave you food," she didn't say about cooks coming and giving food. She said that they received it and I don't know if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In any way, she has stated -- she has answered the question saying "no," so no harm done. Let's proceed, Mr. Doria. But you are right she never qualified those persons as cooks. That's Mr. Jones who is doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, we can perhaps get there by another route. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Assuming that whoever cooks food prefers, so -- would like to see others tasting it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you remember who brought you the food?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If I were to -- I will suggest some names to you and tell me if they ring a bell. Do you remember the name Bahra [phoen]? Bahra.

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Mirfeta [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: There were Muslim women there, were there not, who brought you food every day?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you, in fact, have a clear recollection of these events 12 years ago?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You don't remember the names of any of the Muslim women who brought you food every day?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I won't even wait for an objection, because she has not conceded at any time, Mr. Jones, that Muslim women brought in food with any frequency. I mean, not just every day. This has never been conceded by the witness. It's being put to her by you continuously, and continuously she has been telling you "I don't remember, I don't recollect."

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. Let me put it this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would suggest you move to something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Perhaps one final question. Do you have any recollection of who the people were who brought you food?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Doria.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's a perfectly reasonable question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But I -- I haven't got a clue as to what the objection is likely to be. Yes, Mr. Doria.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: I was thinking the witness already clearly answered to this question saying that, no, she doesn't have a clear recollection of who brought -- specifically who brought her the food, so I don't know if there is any ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, let's take --

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: I don't know if there is any reason coming back again with the same question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Let's take it -- you are partly right. But Madam Stamenic, was the food brought to you and to the other women in the cell where you were staying in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Was it always the same person or persons that brought in the food, or would these persons change from time to time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I think I would leave it at that, there, Mr. Jones and move to the next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's what I sought to establish. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now as far as the water is concerned, again the water which you received might not have been of the best quality, but you did receive water on a daily basis, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And you told us yesterday how you weren't able to wash. But, again, were you told, or did you become aware that there was such a shortage of water in Srebrenica that nobody could wash properly?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't told. I mean, I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, you told us how you were given a log fire and logs -- a stove rather, and logs to keep you warm in the cold winter temperature. Just a question about these logs. Were these heavy logs?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember how big they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, you've told us how men came to your cell carrying logs. Is it right they would be carrying many logs at a time? In other words, they would have their arms full with logs?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember how many they had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What's the relevance of the question? I do relate it to the persons who she testified yesterday were bending down as they carried the logs, but.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Exactly. That's precisely it. The next question will make that clear, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Go ahead --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Ms. Stamenic, you told us how these men who came into the cell were bent over. Was that with the effort of carrying these logs?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if it was because the logs were too heavy, but they were bent over, a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you. Now finally on the conditions, you've told us how you had blankets to sleep on. It was put to you that you didn't have mattresses or pillows. Wasn't it in fact a case of the blankets serving as bedding?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not use any pillows.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. You had a blanket each, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure if all of us had one.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. But most of you?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, most of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. Now, dealing specifically with your treatment in light of your wound, isn't it right that the guards actually came into your cell and actually tried to help to get you walking in order that you wouldn't be immobilised?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody helped me walk.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Was Milenija Mitrovic with you in the cell when you were detained in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You told us that your wounds were only dressed once when you were in the Detention Centre. Isn't it right, in fact, that that in fact occurred more than once, that a nurse came but that also some young girls and boys came to dress your wounds and left bandages with your mother?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we need -- one moment, I think we need to split it in two, because there are two questions in one here, Mr. Jones. Let's put the first question first: Whether -- it's being put to you, Madam Stamenic, that what you told us yesterday is not 100 per cent correct, in that it is being suggested that nurses or a nurse or someone for that matter came to nurse your wounds more than once while you were in the Detention Centre. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It wasn't that the nurse came more than once but that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I said a nurse or someone else for that matter.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A nurse used to come.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. How many times did this nurse come to dress your wounds while were you in the Detention Centre? Can you repeat your answer, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Once. And did anyone else, apart from that nurse, come while you were at the Detention Centre during those 20 days or so to dress your wounds?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The next question, you can put the question yourself, Mr. Jones, or else I can put it for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. I will put it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Weren't bandages also left with your mother so that she could dress your wounds?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's move, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Finally, didn't you also receive painkillers?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Isn't it also true that you received more food because you were injured? In other words, that you actually -- a special portion was made available to you because of your injury?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I got the same thing as the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned how a person who introduced himself as Zulfo came to your cell. And he asked all of you whether anyone mistreated you, and he received the reply that no one had been. That's correct, firstly, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And in fact that was the truth, wasn't it, that no one had mistreated you? Sorry, I will withdraw that question. That has already been answered.

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No physical mistreatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: But you didn't tell him of any other type of mistreatment, did you?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Nor did any of the other women tell him of any other type of mistreatment?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And it's true of him too, isn't it, that you had a clear view of him because you described him to us, and that therefore he too came during the day?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, do you remember a girl called Svetlana Trifunovic?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: She was the daughter of Zivana and who was from Cosici; correct?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And she was, or she at least appeared to be around ten to eleven years old; would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thereabouts, roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now it's right, isn't it, that she wasn't in fact kept in the Detention Centre at night, but was actually kept in the house of a Muslim family?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, they used to take them somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: When you say "they" are you also referring to Branko, the boy?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So Branko and Svetlana did not stay at the Detention Centre at night. They were taken elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Would you agree that Svetlana did not spend a single night at the Detention Centre?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. But certainly you told us she was -- that she and Branko were taken away in the evening. So I put it to you that maybe the maximum she could have stayed there, a night or two at the beginning, but for the rest of the time she was taken elsewhere. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, Svetlana came to the cell with her mother, Zivana after you, didn't she?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really remember how it went.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You don't recall that you were in the cell and that then she came in after you had already arrived?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If she can't remember, let's move, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. If I might refresh her memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If it would assist, I will refresh your memory from your statement which was read to you yesterday. And it says for the record, it is 00998370. Second paragraph. "Later in the evening, Stanija Mitrovic and Milenija Mitrovic, both from my village Kusici, and a woman by the name of Zivana from the village Cosici, Skelani and her ten to eleven years old daughter were also brought to the Detention Centre and kept in the same cell we were." Now hearing that does that refresh your memory as to when, whether she arrived after you were already in the cell?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: She said "da," but again, I don't see the reflection of her answer in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It has come out as "no," in fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: She said "da." I heard her very clearly say "da," which means "yes," and on the transcript now I see "no."

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I can put the question again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Or we can ask her whether she replied yes or no to your previous question, or to your last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you recall now that in fact Svetlana arrived after you were already in the cell?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. And she and her mother were exchanged at the end of January, weren't they, January 1993?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So in fact Svetlana was only in Srebrenica for ten days or so? Maximum two weeks?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat because we can't hear in the booth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Stamenic, could you please repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe a fortnight or ten days, roughly speaking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Did she appear to you to be fine when you saw her, not unduly disturbed or anything?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was frightened.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, you were the only woman in the Detention Centre, in your cell, who had actually been wounded in the thigh, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: There was no one else who had any gun shot wound or any fracture or any serious injury?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Do you recall that when you were exchanged, a Serb called Branislav Gligic received you on the Serb side?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The name is Branislav Gligic?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well do you remember someone by the nickname Pira? Pira?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It has not been interpreted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It has been interpreted as "Pira."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well do you at least remember that when you were exchanged, the Serb, upon receiving -- upon receiving you dressed your wounds with alcohol? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I would like to go into private session just for two questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go into private session for a couple of questions, and we will return to public -- to open session soon after.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, these questions go to the credit of another witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session now.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now just going back to Zulfo for a moment. You also didn't know that person before the war, did you? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And so you didn't recognise him as someone you knew?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And it's right, isn't it, that you've never been asked to identify this person from either an identity parade or from a set of photographs?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, what? You've never been asked, in other words? Do you confirm that you were never asked to identify this person in one way or another?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was not asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And the same is true of the person whom you described as introducing himself as Naser Oric, you've never been asked to identify that person by photographs or in an identity parade?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. Now, when this person who introduced himself as Naser Oric came to the cell, you told us that he asked whether you received food and then said that, in effect, they themselves didn't get any better, the food. Would it be right to say this person appeared to be concerned about the welfare of all of you?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as soon as he asked us, I gathered that he was concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And when he said "We don't get any better," did you understand that as an expression of regret, that it wasn't possible to give more food? Or that there wasn't more food around for everyone?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: He only said "we are not getting any better ourselves." He did not specify who he meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, he asked, didn't he, about the food you were receiving and he asked why you were in a stretcher?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So it's right that he didn't seem to know how you came to be injured, firstly?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And he didn't seem to know --

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Your Honour ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment, Mr. Jones. Yes, Mr. Doria.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have an objection in relation to the question that my learned colleague put concerning whether the witness knew if the person who introduced himself as Naser Oric had any knowledge about her injury before.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I said "he didn't seem to know." It's clear if one reads the transcript, it really is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: I would say it is speculation, because ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. It's a question directed as to whether she could make an assessment there and then as to his prior knowledge of the cause of her injury, so what's the problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Well, what I mean, Your Honour, is that the fact that someone is asking if you are injured, it doesn't mean that you don't know if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It means that from the question you should be able to assess whether that person knows already what caused the injury or whether he is just playing around. This is what is basically what the question was all about.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Would you agree that, equally, he didn't seem to know how much you and the other women were being fed?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Would you agree --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you rephrase it, it will be better, Mr. Jones, because as it is, it may be a little bit confusing.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: When this person asked how much food you were receiving or whether you were receiving food, did you understand from that that he didn't know whether you were receiving food or not, or how much?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: He asked us whether we received any food.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So to summarise, would you agree that he didn't appear to know very much, if indeed anything, about the regime in the detention cell?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know whether he knew, or whether he didn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's put a direct question. Would you agree, Madam Stamenic, that basically this person, who came into your cell and introduced himself as Naser Oric, was actually coming there to check things out, to see what the conditions were, what food was being given to you, and that sort of thing? Was he checking things out? Is that the impression that you formed in your mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That wasn't really the gist of my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know. But I think at the end of the day that is what is important, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It is whether he appeared to be ignorant of the workings of the cell. That is the question I would like her to answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will come to that later. Let's see this first.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether he knew, or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's fine. I will move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we can move. It's basically we can't proceed, we can't get more of the witness on this point, I think, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's simply this, he didn't appear very well informed, did he, of what was going on?

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think this is what the witness has just answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think I have to sustain your objection, and let's move to the next question, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well a few more -- a few final questions, although I'm not quite sure if we will be able to conclude by the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's not a problem. The next witness, who will be with us for a few days, at least, to say the least, can start at any time after the break. Will he be testifying with the protective measures?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's something we're going to clarify during the break. There might be a change.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, all right. Thank you. So you think there will be a change? Or there might be a change?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: It appears that there will be a change.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm saying, because there is in the gallery a considerable number of students from Ireland, and I know that they are quite interested in these proceedings. So it will be of great interest for them to follow the next witness, who is one of the key witnesses in this trial. Yes, Mr. Jones. Take your time. I mean, I'm not telling you please wind-up in three minutes or four minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No. I will probably go ten or fifteen minutes into the next session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's not a problem at all, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm going to turn to a different area altogether now, which is the sounds which you say you heard of men being beaten. Now, firstly, that wasn't something you heard every night, was it?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: You say that you heard those sounds every night? And I think you said -- I will need to check the transcript from yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: She said "twice a night," Mr. Jones. "Twice a night," yesterday, that's what she said.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So is that your evidence, that every night there was a regular periodic sound of beatings which occurred twice on each occasion?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember whether this happened every night.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well that was precisely my point, Ms. Stamenic, and we need to be very -- very clear about this. You do not recall, do you, that there was a sound of beatings every single night that you were in the cell?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could hear sounds, but I don't remember whether I heard them every night.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Including sounds of people moaning? In other words, did these sounds which you heard include sounds of people moaning and generally making sounds of misery, which are consistent with not being beaten at that moment?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard moaning and wailing.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I put it to you that in terms of the sound of people actually being struck, that that in fact only occurred on one night and that that wasn't repeated. Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard moaning and wailing. I don't know whether this happened every night, whether they were beaten every night. I only know that I heard them moan and wail.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. You accept that people can moan and wail when they're not being beaten?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Finally, and I don't wish to dwell on this subject at any length, but you referred to hearing the sound of bats, I think you said, being used on people. Now, firstly, you were on your stretcher the whole time, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard sticks, or bats. That's what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Now, you didn't have your ear against the wall, did you?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I put it to you that the very most that you could have heard would have been of muffled sounds of some form of impact, but you couldn't possibly hear something which you could distinguish as the sound of a stick being used. Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: It sounded to me like the sound of a stick or a bat. I don't know whether it was a stick or something else. I didn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Jones, and Mr. Doria, I am suggesting to you and to the interpreters and the technicians and the rest to go on and finish with the testimony of this witness and then have the break after provided we do not exceed 15 minutes or so, if that is agreeable. If you prefer to have the break now, we will then have the break now and resume immediately after. What is your preference.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I can be finished in five minutes, so my preference would be to continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Doria, is there re-examination in the offing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So what I suggest, then, is, if it's convenient for you, that we break now an we will resume in 25 minutes' time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Well I had one question on this subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, yes, finish that one question and we will reconvene in 25 minutes' time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Ms. Stamenic you told us just now that you said you heard what sounded to you like the sound of a stick, or a bat; that you didn't know whether it was a stick or something else. You didn't see anything. Do you accept that you could have been mistaken about the sounds which you heard, when you say that they were those of a bat? In other words, do you accept that --

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether I'm mistaken. I wouldn't say. I heard those sounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you. We can take the break there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I thank you, Mr. Jones. Mrs. Stamenic, we are going to have a 25- to 30-minute break now. I am sure that our staff over there where you are at the moment will give you all the assistance that you require so that you can have a decent break. After the break, you will be testifying for approximately 15 to 20 minutes and then you are free to go. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's re-establish contact via videolink with the witness and try to finish so that we can start with the next witness immediately after. Yes, it seems that we have established contact. I just want to know, from you, Madam Stamenic, whether you can see us as clear as we can see you and whether you are receiving interpretation of what I am saying in your own language.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, madam. Let's proceed, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, just a few final questions from me anyway, Ms. Stamenic. And firstly, to clarify something which might also be a problem of interpretation. When you were asked yesterday, when you heard sounds of screaming, you said and I believe the expression in B/C/S was "dva put nocu." Now did you mean to say you heard that twice a night? Or whether you heard that twice during your stay in detention and that it happened at night?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Twice during the time of my detention.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, turning finally to your exchange on the 6th of February, 1993, you and the other Serbs were exchanged for dead Muslims, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: In fact, I think you even knew the number, that it was ten, ten dead Muslims?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how many there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And how many of you - live people - were exchanged for them? Approximately?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some 20 or so. 15 or 20, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And there wasn't a single live Muslim who was returned to the Muslim side; would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see any.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: On another subject now. You don't recall, do you, giving any statement in 1994 about these events, do you?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave a statement in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. Now, you know Ilija Ivanovic, don't you? You knew him before the war, firstly?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And you still know him. You still see him?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Jones. Mr. Doria, re-examination, if at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. A couple of questions. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, you testified yesterday that when you were captured and you were brought to your house, you saw soldiers and civilians. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: You testified yesterday that when you were captured, you were taken to your house and then you saw the -- all the soldiers and civilians. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we were exchanged or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: No. At the time when you were captured, I mean on the 16th January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: You testified that you saw civilians going into your house and taking items from there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Did you see the soldiers, those that you saw, people in military uniform, stopping those civilians from doing that?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I don't know how that arises from cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Correct. Objection sustained, Mr. Doria.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Let me rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You could have asked that question during your examination-in-chief, because you did actually ask the witness who was taking things out, whether it included also the soldiers, and she answered "no," and you could have easily put that question, that additional question to the witness then. But certainly it doesn't arise now out of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, you testified yesterday as having seen a woman Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. under the name of Djemila, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: And was that woman at 6.00 also in front of your house?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was in front of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: And is that also true, that a postman was also in front of your house?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, you were put a question yesterday, or an allegation was made by my learned colleague to the effect that the group that you saw was indeed a group of fighters, and which were together civilians and soldiers. What impression you got from that group?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, that is not how I put it at all. It was that they were all mixed you up together in the same place at the same time. Not that they constituted a discrete group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. And in addition, Mr. Jones and Mr. Doria, at least the way I understood it yesterday when you were putting this to the witness, Mr. Jones, is the description of fighters arose, after that the witness agreed that she didn't know at all whether this was a proper army, whether there was an organised group of soldiers under a proper command. And then it was put to her that these were better described then as fighters.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then amongst the other questions that were put and were answered is whether civilians also were carrying arms. But at no time it was put to the witness, by Mr. Jones, that the description of fighters included both civilians and soldiers. I took it as meaning only soldiers or those wearing uniforms and carrying weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, that was right, at least in the context of the Muslim army being better described as soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Arising out of that, of course, you can put any question you like provided it is within the parameters of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Madam Stamenic, the group that you saw mixed, soldiers and civilians, can you recall which group was the biggest one? Did see more soldiers or more civilians?

utterances.speaker: Stana Stamenic [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Stamenic, you testified yesterday that certain items, and specifically you told us about the blankets that were put into the cart, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Again, I didn't raise any --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, there were things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead, finish your answer, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were things, but I don't know whether those blankets had been taken out of my house and put on the cart. But in any case, there were things when I was put on the cart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't go into the question at all of removal of items from her house in cross-examination, so, again, same objection, that this did not arise. And it is indicative my learned friend keeps referring to matters which she said in examination-in-chief rather than cross-examination. It illustrates the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. DORIA
utterances.text: Your Honour, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
